main_body: Flat-roofed desert adobe house: a large sand-coloured roof terrace (with rug and hatch) above a clay front wall with an arched door and a lattice window
top_band: Light tan roof surface with speckles, rows ~2-30, with a raised parapet rim at the sides and a lighter front lip at rows 28-31
evidence: Down the middle column, the light tan roof surface (rows ~2-30) is followed by a lighter lip at rows ~29-31 and a dark brown eave line at rows ~32-33. Below that is the terracotta wall (rows 34-63) with crenellation shadow notches, a cream-framed arched door and a lattice window with a sill. The roof is a clearly horizontal surface, with its parapet and the rug and hatch lying on it, so both a top and a front face are drawn. The door is only moderately inset, but the eave shadow and front-edge line carry the construction.

style.flat_fills_note: only the small rug centre is flat
style.evidence: The outline is dark brown, tinted to match the adobe, not near-black. The roof and wall carry speckle, grain and per-pixel variation in about 4 tones each, plus a striped wooden door with studs and a lattice window, so the surfaces are not flat. It lacks the 5-6 step ramps and tile scallops of the references, and the rug interior is a flat block, so density is slightly lower. It is still acceptable beside the references for a plastered desert building.
